milestones.title: Product foundation and data sources
milestones.scope: Start the product in its own git repository, in the workspace subfolder energy-forecast/, with its language, layout and test setup recorded in docs/decisions.md, and docs/known-limitations.md started. The configuration holds the site (location, time zone, solar peak power), the Prometheus URL and one PromQL query per signal (grid import and export, solar, battery, heating, indoor and outdoor temperature), so that the home's real metric names only touch the configuration. Read these signals from Prometheus onto a common 15-minute local-time grid, handling gaps and daylight saving time, and fetch the next 24 hours of temperature and solar/cloud forecast from a public weather service. Use answers/R1.md if it exists; the real Prometheus is not needed here. Done when one command prints these series from a configuration, the README says how to install and run it, and tests cover both sources from recorded or synthetic responses, without network.

tasks.title: Plan the milestone
criteria: plan.json holds the milestone's tasks after this one, each small enough for one session, with a kind, checkable criteria (the behaviour, the tests that show it, the docs) and the note topics to read
Each task whose order matters names the tasks it needs in after
The last task closes the milestone: a review of the whole milestone, the docs and the known limitations
tasks.summary: Planned M2 into M2.2 (repository, layout, test setup, configuration), M2.3 (15-minute local-time grid, DST, gaps), M2.4 (Prometheus reader), M2.5 (Open-Meteo forecast), M2.6 (the one command and the README) and M2.7 (closing review). Added notes/environment.md and notes/data-sources.md, with the facts probed for the plan: the machine's Python 3.10 without tomllib, and Open-Meteo's local times that ignore daylight saving. No task waits on R1 or R2: M2 runs on synthetic data, and the product stays committed locally until R2 is answered.

tasks.title: Start the product: repository, layout, test setup and configuration
tasks.details: Create energy-forecast/ as its own git repository. Python is the expected language (simple numeric fits in M3, a Prometheus client in M4); the session decides and records why. R2 is open, so there is no remote: when answers/R2.md exists, add the remote and push; otherwise commit locally and say so in the summary. When answers/R1.md exists, use its facts in the example configuration; otherwise use placeholder metric names. Signals: grid_import, grid_export, solar, battery, heating, indoor_temperature, outdoor_temperature.
criteria: energy-forecast/ is a git repository of its own with the work committed, and the workspace's .gitignore names it, so that git add . from the workspace stages neither its files nor a gitlink

docs/decisions.md records the language and its minimum version, each dependency with its reason, the layout, the test setup and the configuration format; docs/known-limitations.md exists and names the missing remote while R2 is open
The product installs into a new virtual environment with one documented command, and the test suite runs from there without network
Loading a configuration file gives the site (latitude, longitude, time zone, solar peak power), the Prometheus URL and one PromQL query for each of the seven signals
Tests show that a valid file loads, and that a missing field, an unknown signal, an unknown time zone, an out-of-range latitude and a negative peak power each give an error naming the field

An example configuration in the repository states the unit and sign of each signal (power in W, temperature in °C, the battery's sign), a test loads it, and no metric name appears in the code outside configuration and test data
tasks.summary: Started energy-forecast/ as its own git repository, committed locally only: R2 is open, so it has no remote, as docs/known-limitations.md says. The workspace's .gitignore names it. Python 3.10 or later, with the choices in docs/decisions.md; src/energy_forecast/config.py gives load_config, whose ConfigError names the field; config.example.toml has placeholder site values and metric names (R1 is open) and states each signal's unit and sign; tests/conftest.py fails any test that connects beyond loopback. 80 tests pass, also under unshare -rn. One thing differs from what criterion 3 suggests: the documented install command fails with this machine's system Python, which lacks python3.10-venv (M2.1's note wrongly had it working, now corrected). I could not install that package, so R3 asks for it, with no task waiting on it. I checked the command as written from a fresh clone with pyenv's base 3.12.13, used read-only in a temporary folder despite the note's advice against pyenv; on the system 3.10.12, only the pip half of the command ran, in an environment made with virtualenv, which is the energy-forecast/.venv that later sessions use.

tasks.title: The common 15-minute local-time grid
tasks.details: One small module that both sources use. Slots are defined on UTC instants and their local time comes from the site's time zone; a slot is labelled by its start and covers the 15 minutes after it. Missing values stay visible, so that M3 and later analysis can tell measured values from filled ones.
criteria: A function gives the slots of a time range in the site's time zone, each with its UTC instant and its local time with UTC offset, aligned on :00, :15, :30 and :45 local
Tests for Europe/Brussels show 96 slots on an ordinary day, 92 on 2026-03-29 with no local 02:xx slot, and 100 on 2026-10-25 with 02:00 twice, told apart by their offsets +02:00 and +01:00

A function places timestamped samples on the slots: samples within one slot are averaged, samples outside the range are ignored, and a slot without a sample holds an explicit missing value, never zero; tests include an empty input

Runs of missing slots up to a limit from the configuration are filled by linear interpolation and flagged as filled, and longer runs stay missing; tests cover a run at the limit, one past it, runs at the start and end of the series (not filled) and a run across a daylight saving change
docs/decisions.md records the slot's label convention, the representation of a missing value and the gap rule

tasks.title: Read the signals from Prometheus onto the grid
tasks.details: One query_range per configured signal, evaluated at the slots' ends, so that avg_over_time(x[15m]) lands on the slot that it covers. Tests use synthetic responses in the format of the Prometheus HTTP API, from a fake transport or a loopback server: the real Prometheus is not needed. Use answers/R1.md if it exists.
criteria: For a range of slots, the reader calls /api/v1/query_range once per signal with a 15-minute step and returns one grid series per signal; a test checks the query, start, end and step sent, and that a value evaluated at a slot's end lands on the slot that starts 15 minutes earlier
A range of more than 11,000 steps is split into several requests; a test over 120 days finds every slot exactly once

Absent samples and the values NaN and +Inf become missing slots, and a query with an empty result gives an all-missing series with a warning naming the signal; tests include a gap and a range across 2026-10-25
An unreachable server, a timeout, a non-200 reply, a body with status error and a query returning more than one series each give an error naming the signal and its query, with a test for each
The docs say how to write a signal's query (avg_over_time for gauges, rate for counters, clamp_min for one signed metric, unit conversion), and the example configuration uses these forms
The tests reach no network beyond loopback

tasks.title: Fetch the next 24 hours of weather forecast onto the grid
tasks.details: Open-Meteo is the expected service: no key, 15-minute data (see the note for its traps). The fetch takes the slots that it must fill, not a fixed 'next 24 hours', because M3's solar factor will also ask for past values; build no history feature now. The service's URL has a default, and the configuration can override it for tests.
criteria: For the site's latitude and longitude, the fetch returns temperature (°C), cloud cover (%) and solar radiation (W/m²) as grid series over the next 96 slots, from the first slot boundary after now
Times come from unix timestamps, never from the service's local strings; a test with a recorded response across 2026-10-25 puts each value on its slot, with local 02:xx appearing twice
A test with known values shows a radiation mean stamped T on the slot that starts at T-15min, and temperature and cloud cover stamped T on the slot that starts at T

An unreachable service, a timeout and an HTTP error with its reason each give an error that carries the reason; a null value, an absent variable or a response too short give missing slots with a warning; a test for each
Tests run from a real response recorded in the test data, plus synthetic ones, without network

docs/decisions.md records the choice of service, with its terms of use, and docs/known-limitations.md records its limits, such as 15-minute data being interpolated outside Central Europe and North America

tasks.title: One command prints the series from a configuration
criteria: One command, given a configuration file and a number of past days, prints the Prometheus signals over the past range and the weather forecast over the next 24 hours, one row per slot, with the local time and UTC offset and one column per series, missing values empty and filled values flagged; the README documents this format
The command gives each series' counts of measured, filled and missing slots on stderr, so that stdout stays parseable
When one source fails, the message names it, the other source is still printed and the exit code is non-zero; an invalid configuration gives its message and a non-zero exit code; tests show both

An end-to-end test runs the command against fake Prometheus and weather servers on loopback, their URLs from the configuration, and checks the printed rows, including a gap and a range across a daylight saving change
The README says how to install on a new machine, write the configuration, run the command and run the tests, with sample output from a real run of the command

tasks.title: Close the milestone: review against the scope, docs and known limitations
criteria: Each sentence of M2's scope is checked against the product, what falls short is fixed, and the summary gives the result
The README's install and run steps were followed from a fresh clone in a new virtual environment, and the whole test suite passes there with the outside network blocked
The command was run once against the real weather service, and the fields of its response match the response recorded in the test data, or the recording and the code are updated

docs/decisions.md holds the milestone's significant choices, and docs/known-limitations.md says what is left: no run against a real Prometheus (R1), the placeholder metric names, and the missing remote while R2 is open

milestones.title: First complete 24-hour forecast
milestones.scope: The simplest model for every input of VISION.md, before improving any of them: household use by time of week from the history, without the heating; a thermal model fitted from the indoor and outdoor temperatures with the heating off and with it on; heating active and heating power over the next 24 hours from the temperature forecast; solar generation from the solar/cloud forecast, scaled by a factor fitted on the history. Combine them into a forecast per 15 minutes of household use, heating, solar and net grid power before the battery, flagging the slots above the capacity tariff's limit (2.5 kW by default). Done when one command outputs this forecast with all its intermediate values in a documented format, and each model has tests on synthetic data with a known answer. Battery control and the electric car stay out.

milestones.title: Forecast service, metrics and archive
milestones.scope: Run the forecast as a service, on a schedule. It exports every internal value and intermediate prediction (forecast solar, forecast temperature, forecast heating active, fitted parameters, run status) as Prometheus metrics, with a documented catalogue, and archives each run so that any prediction can be compared later with what happened. It offers the latest forecast in a documented form that the future battery control can read. When Prometheus or the weather service fails, it retries, keeps the last good forecast and shows its age in a metric, rather than stopping. Done when the docs say how to install and configure it on a new machine, and tests cover the schedule, the archive, the failure paths and a scrape of the metrics from a service run against fake sources.

milestones.title: Forecast against reality
milestones.scope: Measure the forecast. Compare the archived forecasts with what happened, per intermediate value (solar, temperature, heating active, household use, net grid power) and per horizon, with the error and the bias exported as metrics and given by a report command. A backtest replays the models over past history, beside a naive reference (the same slot a week before), so that quality can be judged without waiting weeks. A dashboard definition shows forecast against actual. Done when the report, the backtest and the dashboard are documented, and tests on synthetic data with known errors check the figures.

milestones.title: Run on the home's data and improve the weakest part
milestones.scope: Needs request R1: the session that plans this milestone puts it in the waiting_on of the tasks that need the real data. Point the service and the backtest at the home's Prometheus, fix what real data breaks (units, signs, gaps, short retention), and check that the fitted thermal and solar parameters are plausible. Then, from the backtest, improve the one or two parts that cause the largest error on the 15-minute net grid forecast, keeping the code simple. Done when the docs hold the backtest results on real data before and after the changes, and docs/known-limitations.md says what is left.

milestones.title: Plan the next milestones
milestones.scope: Plan the next milestones from VISION.md, FEEDBACKS.md, the product's docs/known-limitations.md and history/README.md.

requests.title: Access to the home's Prometheus, and the facts of the site
requests.request: Sessions cannot reach the home's data: nothing answers at localhost:9090 on the machine that runs them, and VISION.md gives no address or metric names. Please give: (1) a Prometheus URL reachable from that machine, read-only is enough, or else an export of the signals below covering several weeks; (2) the metric name, unit and sign for grid import and export, solar generation, battery charge and discharge, heating power or heating on/off, indoor temperature and outdoor temperature, and how far back the history goes; (3) the home's location for the weather forecast (the nearest town is enough) and the solar panels' peak power, with their orientation if known. M2 to M5 can go on without it, on synthetic data with the metric names in the configuration; M6, which runs on the real data, cannot.

requests.title: The product's remote, and VISION.md's wording
requests.request: M2 starts the product in its own git repository, in the workspace subfolder energy-forecast/. WORKFLOW.md asks to push it, and no remote exists. Please give the URL of an empty repository that sessions can push to, or allow them to create a private one under the account of the workspace's remote. Until then the product is only committed locally, and would be lost with this machine. Also, for VISION.md, which sessions may not edit: WORKFLOW.md says that it names the folders, so please add energy-forecast/ there. Its lines on a 'launcher' and on 'libraries listed below' look left over from a template: sessions read 'launcher' as the forecast service and take no library as suggested; please correct VISION.md if that is wrong.

requests.title: Install python3.10-venv on the machine that runs the sessions
requests.request: Please run `sudo apt install python3.10-venv` on that machine. The product's documented install command, `python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -e '.[test]'`, fails there with the system Python because `ensurepip` is missing, and installing a system package needs root, so no session can do it. Sessions can go on without it, with a virtual environment made by virtualenv (see notes/environment.md), so no task waits on this; once it is done, the command works there as the README says.
